title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to Us Than to the Pyramids

segments.text: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The Great Pyramid was already about 2,500 years old when she was born.
To Cleopatra, the pyramids were ancient history too.
She ruled as Egypt's last active pharaoh.
So when you picture ancient Egypt, she came at the very end.
Closer to us than to the pyramids she stood beside.
Follow for history they never taught you.

description: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid's construction. Follow for daily history!

title: Oxford University Is Older Than the Aztec Empire

segments.text: Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire even existed.
Teaching at Oxford began around the year 1096.
The Aztec capital wasn't founded until 1325.
That's more than two centuries later.
So while Oxford held lectures, the Aztec Empire hadn't begun.
A university older than an entire empire.
Follow for history they never taught you.

description: Oxford was teaching students 200+ years before the Aztec Empire was even founded. Follow for daily history!

title: Australia Once Lost a War Against Birds

segments.text: In 1932, Australia declared war on emus, and lost.
Thousands of emus were destroying farmers' crops.
So the army was sent in with machine guns.
But the emus scattered and were too fast to hit.
After weeks, the soldiers gave up.
A war against birds, that the birds won.
Follow for history they never taught you.

title: The Library That Burned for Centuries

segments.text: The Library of Alexandria didn't burn down in a single night.
It declined slowly over centuries, through fires, cuts and neglect.
At its peak it may have held hundreds of thousands of scrolls.
Scholars from across the ancient world came to study there.
When it was gone, knowledge that took centuries to gather was lost.
And we still don't know everything it once contained.
Follow for history they never taught you.

description: The Library of Alexandria didn't vanish in one fire - it faded over centuries. Follow for daily history!

title: How a Forgotten Kingdom Ruled the Mediterranean

segments.text: The Kingdom of Tyre was once a bustling trade hub.
Its Phoenician merchants traveled across the Mediterranean.
They were the first to develop the alphabet we use today.
Tyre's purple dye was worth more than gold.
Its unmatched naval power even challenged empires.
But, like many great civilizations, it eventually faded.
The Kingdom of Tyre was a beacon of progress.
The Kingdom of Tyre was once a bustling trade hub.
Follow for history they never taught you.

title: The Five-Year War That Changed History

segments.text: In 1870, France fought a war over a piece of land.
The Franco-Prussian War started over a diplomatic dispute.
It led to the rise of the German Empire.
Paris fell to the Prussians after a brutal siege.
The conflict ended with drastic territorial changes.
France lost Alsace-Lorraine, a blow to national pride.
This war forged modern Europe’s power dynamics.
In 1870, France fought a war over a piece of land.
Follow for history they never taught you.

title: The Queen Who Ruled Without a King

segments.text: Eleanor of Aquitaine was one of the most powerful women.
She married two kings and ruled two countries.
Eleanor was a key player in the Crusades.
At times, she even led her own armies into battle.
Her influence stretched from France to England.
Eleanor's legacy shaped European politics for generations.
Eleanor of Aquitaine was one of the most powerful women.
Follow for history they never taught you.

title: The Invention That Changed Warfare Forever

segments.text: The crossbow revolutionized military tactics in the middle ages.
Its power allowed average soldiers to pierce armor.
Used by peasants, it leveled the playing field.
Warlords feared its silent strike.
King Richard I of England favored its use in battles.
Warfare would never be the same again.
The crossbow revolutionized military tactics in the middle ages.

title: The Ship That Never Came Back

segments.text: In 1913, a luxury yacht vanished without a trace.
The sailing yacht, known as the ‘Wanderer,’ was perfect for adventure.
It set out from New York, bound for the Caribbean.
After weeks with no word, a search party was launched.
Only debris was found - no survivors.
This mysterious loss captivated the nation.
The ship ‘Wanderer’ vanished without a trace.
